title: Profile module
summary: Registers accounts and edits user profiles with UUID-aware registration and task-generated IDs.
requirements: Register a username and create its profile.
Reject a different UUID for a username that is already owned.
Apply requested profile edits without replacing other fields.
nonfunctional: Process registration by username ownership; key profile records by generated user ID.
constraints: The source accepts a repeated registration with the same UUID and creates a new ID; it does not return a stable ID.
invariants: The first registration stores username ownership and emits a generated ID.
Only edited fields change after registration.
acceptance: Registration, conflicts, ID and profile readback, and field edits work after a processing barrier.
Repeated registration with the same UUID matches the source behavior.
environment: Rama stream module with registration and edit depots.
decisions: The registration depot hashes by username; the edit depot hashes by user ID.
tradeoffs: UUID checks username ownership; it is not a durable idempotency key.
etls: profiles stream: claims username, generates an ID, writes the profile, and expands field edits.
queries: No query topology; client directly selects $$profiles by user ID.

write: Registration routes by username; the accepted path records UUID and ID, then hashes the generated ID to write the profile.
Edit events hash by user ID, expand requested fields, and update the profile.
read: Client directly selects the profile by user ID.
flow.partition: Username ownership and user profile are on different hashed owners; accepted registration relocates by generated ID.

caveat: Same UUID append generates a fresh user ID in the source, and can leave the earlier profile record behind. This behavior is tested rather than corrected.

title: REST API integration module
summary: Fetches response bodies asynchronously with a task-scoped HTTP client and stores the latest body for each URL.
requirements: Send HTTP GET requests without blocking the caller.
Store the latest response body for each URL.
Close HTTP client resources at the end of their lifecycle.
nonfunctional: Stream processing waits for each asynchronous GET to complete. No latency or retry guarantee is made.
constraints: Tests use a disposable local HTTP fixture; they do not depend on a public API.
The source extracts a body from completed NettyResponse without checking status. Transport exceptions fail processing and trigger retries.
invariants: The response PState is keyed by requested URL.
acceptance: Read local response bodies after processing.
Keep the body from completed non-2xx HTTP responses.
environment: Rama stream ETL, AsyncHttpClient task global, local HTTP test server.
decisions: Hash by URL for depot ownership; $$responses is keyed by URL.
A CompletableFuture passes the HTTP response into the topology.
tradeoffs: The source does not set a timeout or response-size limit, or check status. Retry bounds are unverified.
seam: The tests use a loopback HTTP fixture only.
etls: get-http stream waits for the HTTP result asynchronously and extracts the response body.
queries: No query topology; client directly selects response by URL.

write: A GET request enters the URL-hashed depot; the task-local client returns a future; the completed response body replaces the stored value for that URL.
read: The client selects the latest stored body directly.
flow.partition: URL hash aligns source event with same URL response record.

caveat: The source establishes task-scoped client creation, closing, and body extraction, but does not establish transport retry count.

title: Music catalog migration
summary: Updates a catalog module to migrate album song strings into parsed records and index new data in that format.
requirements: Index old albums with song strings before the update.
Migrate old PState values during the module update.
Parse songs added after the update and preserve values across repeated updates and reads.
nonfunctional: The challenge covers one A-to-B module lifecycle.
constraints: The parser is case-sensitive, splits on ft/feat markers, and uses only the first two segments.
invariants: Album artist/name keys persist across the schema update.
Structured song records retain song names and featured artist values.
acceptance: Old and new album records return structured songs after the update.
Repeated updates and reads preserve migrated data.
environment: Two generations of one Rama module name; albums microbatch topology.
decisions: Albums are keyed by artist, then subindexed by album name.
Migration wraps the new album schema with ID parse-song-data.
tradeoffs: The parser does not cover the full music-title grammar; an already-new first song bypasses conversion.
seam: The lifecycle adapter binds the client to a stable module name.
etls: albums microbatch writes album values and parses input for the new generation.
queries: No query topology; the client selects an album directly by artist and album name.

write: Album events hash by artist and index subindexed album names.
The update migrates old values in place; the new-generation ETL parses strings before indexing.
read: The client selects an album by artist and title.
flow.partition: Artist owns the album subtree; album name is a subindexed child key.

caveat: The A-to-B update and protocol/client continuity form one lifecycle. The parser follows the source and is not a complete feature-credit parser.
